{{Version|2.2.23}}
[[File:Arch Button.png|frameless|left]]
Archaeology is a menu that unlocks at Obelisk Level 30. You beat blocks to gain fragments. You can spend them on [[Archaeology#Upgrades|Upgrades]] to improve Archaeology, and on [[Archaeology#Idols|Idols]] that provide bonuses to the main game.

{{clear|left}}
==In-game description==
<div style="margin:auto;font-size:0.9em">
{{Quote
|quote = 
In this menu your miner will permanently mine blocks to gather fragments and archaeology experience!     

Archaeology will constantly be running in the background - regardless of whether this menu is open or not! You accumulate one attack per second when offline and process them all on login!

Experience levels up your Archaeology level, granting you stat points to spec into one of 5 skills in the upgrade menu.  

Depending on your goals you can adjust your stat points loadout, play about with these as much as you like! Removing Agility stat points will deplete your current stamina by the same amount Agility grants.  

There are Dirt, Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Mythic Blocks - Common+ Blocks drop fragments which can be used on either Archaeology upgrades or summoning Idols!

Idols - Use fragments to summon powerful Idols, these grant stat buffs that will help you progress in the game! Every idol requires a task to be completed in order for their bonus to activate.     

Game Speed does not affect this menu!
}}</div>

==Strategy==
{{See also|Guides/Archaeology_Guide}}

Unless otherwise noted, this applies specifically for <code>{{Sprite|Ascension||20x20|Ascension 0}}</code>, i.e. initial access to the Archaeology menu.

Starting out: Put enough points into <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Strength||20x20|Strength}}</code> to reach 90 <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Flat Damage||20x20|Damage}}</code> in order to one-shot <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Tier 1 Dirt||20x20|Tier 1 Dirt}}</code> blocks, then invest remaining points into <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Agility||20x20|Agility}}</code> to push your <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Highest Stage||20x20|Highest Stage}}</code>. 

As you get more upgrades you can move more points from Strength into <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Agility||20x20|Agility}}</code>.

Level 35+ Alternate between two builds:
* <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Luck||20x20|Luck}}</code> Setup: Max Luck, rest in Strength. Farms more fragments and experience.
* <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Strength||20x20|Strength}}</code> Setup: Enough Strength to 1-hit dirt blocks, rest in Agility. Reaches higher stages and higher fragment types.

Farm with Luck setup, then push stages with Strength setup. Important after unlocking the <code>{{Sprite|Block Bonker|Skill-Tree#Skills|20x20|Block Bonker}}</code> skill. If you want lower effort gameplay, stay with pure Luck setup.

* <code>Level 50+</code> Modified Luck setup for pushing stages: Max Luck, the rest half/half into Strength and Agility. Balances fragment gain and stage progression.
* <code>Level 55</code> (optional): Farm fragments to max <code>{{Sprite|Minos Idol||20x20|Minos}}</code> and <code>{{Sprite|Dionysus Idol||20x20|Dionysus}}</code> idols early for huge boost in general game progression.
* <code>Level 60</code>: Modified Luck setup for pushing stages: Max Luck,  the rest into Strength. RNG is a big Factor but will always yield a higher Stage than Agility. 
* <code>Level 100</code>: Max Luck and <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Perception||20x20|Perception}}</code>, and put remaining points into Strength. This stops you from going above stage 100 too often, where Block stats increase but rewards (including <code>{{Sprite|Block Bonker|Skill-Tree#Skills|20x20|Block Bonker}}</code> scaling) do not, until you can reliably reach Stage 115+ consistently for <code>{{Sprite|Dino Quest|Pets#Quests|20x20|Dino's Pet Quest}}</code>.

Max [[Archaeology#Upgrades|Upgrades]] before buying [[Archaeology#Idols|Idols]]! (Exception: <code>{{Sprite|Minos Idol||20x20|Minos}}</code> and <code>{{Sprite|Dionysus Idol||20x20|Dionysus}}</code>) [[Archaeology#Idols|Idol]] effects are incremental and maxing [[Archaeology#Upgrades|Upgrades]] is better in the long run.

<code>{{Sprite|Supply Drop|Founder#Supply drop|16x20|Founder Supply Drops}}</code> have an <code>{{Sprite|Arch Icon||20x20|Archaeology Banked Seconds}}</code>  component that scales via <code>{{Sprite|Archaeology Highest Stage||20x20|Archaeology Highest Stage}}</code>. Whenever you get a major power up, try to do a Full Luck, Full Strength, Rest Agility build to increase your banked second gain.

==Archaeology Levels==
Archaeology levels provide the Skill points, which are used to upgrade the [[Archaeology#Skills|Archaeology Skills]]. Levels are earned by obtaining experience [[File:Archaeology Exp.png|16x16px]] when destroying the [[Archaeology#Block_Stats|blocks]], each block provides different amount of experience. The amount of experience required for each level increases over time. 

Following table is just an '''example of initial 100 levels''', which is requirement for [[Archaeology#Ascension|Ascension 2]], however, there is no hard cap for archaeology level.
{{CostTable|Archaeology Level|100|1.2|class{{=}}"wikitable text-align-center sticky-header" style{{=}}"font-size:0.90em"|formula|10|Archaeology Exp| |formula=baseCost*(costScaling^(n+1))|rounding=round}}

===Archaeology Levels Calculation===
The experience needed to advance to next level is calculated with following formula:

<math>Experience(n) = 10 \times 1.2^{n+1}</math>, where <math>n</math> is the current level.

==Skills==
Skills are the basic character attributes available in Archaeology that improve different stats. Each skill provides specific bonuses related to that skill such as increased damage, better loot chances, or faster progression. Skill points are used to upgrade specific skills and they are obtained by leveling up, which requires experience gained by destroying [[Archaeology#Block_Stats|blocks]]. Skill's effects and cap can be further increased by certain [[Archaeology#Upgrades|upgrades]]. Divination and Corruption skills require Ascension to be unlocked.

==Abilities==
Currently there are 3 different abilities available in Archaeology: Enrage, Flurry, and Quake. They offer specific buffs which help progress through the stages. Abilities can also be selected to be automatically used as soon as they come off cooldown. Ability cooldowns as well as the effects/amount of charges can be increased with upgrades.

===Ability Fairy===
[[File:Archaeology Ability Fairy.png|32x32px]] Ability Fairies require [[Archaeology#Ascension|Ascension 2]] [[Archaeology#Ascension_2|upgrade]] to be unlocked. After unlocking they can show up randomly, flying around in the Archaeology window. When interacted with they cause all other abilities to instantly refresh and be used automatically right away.

==Ascension==
Ascension becomes available at [[Obelisk#OB66|Obelisk 66]]. Archaeology prior to ascending is referred to as Ascension 0. Ascension allows for a way to [[#Lost on Ascension|reset progress]] in Archaeology, which in turn unlocks more blocks, skills, upgrades and idols. After ascending you must progress through Ascension 1 to then become eligible for Ascension 2. 

===Ascension 0===
* Gem Upgrades have a max cost of {{Gems|1000}}
* [[Lootbugs#Gem_Buffs|Lootbugs]] give a set number of base<ref name=bugbase>Base amount prior to lootbug multi</ref> archaeology ticks

===Lost on Ascension===
Applies to both Ascension 0->1 and Ascension 1->2
* Archaeology Upgrades
* Archaeology Gem Upgrades
* Banked Archaeology Seconds
* Archaeology Level, Highest Stage 
* (everything except Idols and Idol Tokens)

===Ascension 1===
* Requires Archaeology Level 90, Arch Highest Stage 115, and [[Obelisk#OB66|Obelisk level 66]].
* Divine Blocks now appear, Divinity Skill now available
* Fragment Upgrades become 5x more expensive
* Gem Upgrades become 25x more expensive
* [[Fishing#tabber-Glimmering_Geoduck|Glimmering Geoduck]] fragment bonus capped at +50% (200 Mythic Chests)
* Lootbugs now give base arch ticks based on highest stage, with a cap at stage 200<ref name=lootbug>See [[Lootbugs#Gem_Buffs|here]] for formula </ref>

===Ascension 2===
* Requires Archaeology Level 100 and Highest Stage 150
* Tier 4 Blocks now appear, Corruption Skill now available
* Fragment Upgrades become 10x more expensive<ref name=asccost>Compared to Ascension 0</ref>
* Gem Upgrades become 50x more expensive<ref name=asccost/>
* Glimmering Geoduck fragment bonus capped at +75% (300 Mythic Chests)

<references />

==Mod Chances==
You can see your mod chances and effects in the Stats popup in the Archaeology menu (separate from your other [[Stats|Stats menu]]). When a stage is created, each block rolls your mod chances. For each mod roll that succeeds it's icon appears above the block. When you destroy the block, all mods it has take effect.

{|class="wikitable align-center-1"
! colspan=2 |Mod
!Effect
|-

|3x to 5x Experience from this block
|-
|[[File:Archaeology Loot Mod Chance.png]] ||Loot Mod
|2x to 5x Fragments from this block
|-
|[[File:Archaeology Speed Mod Chance.png]] ||Speed Mod
| +10 to +110 Atk Speed x2
|-
|[[File:Archaeology Stamina Mod Chance.png]] ||Stamina Mod
| +3 to +10 added stamina. (can't go over your max)
|}

==Crosshairs==
===Regular Crosshair===
[[File:Archaeology Crosshair.png|32x32px]] Sometimes when doing Archaeology the Crosshairs can randomly spawn with a 2.2% on top of any block. When that crosshair is tapped, the block that the crosshair was on top of will take damage of same amount as dealt by the miner normally. This also includes a chance to roll a critical hit on the block, same way it normally would for a miner's hit.

===Gold Crosshair===
[[File:Archaeology_Gold_Crosshair.png|32x32px]] Gold Crosshairs are enhanced version of regular Crosshair. They are initially unlocked via [[Archaeology#Luck|Luck skill]] and they greatly multiply the damage dealt by tapping them (base x3).

===Crosshair Auto-Tap===
[[File:Archaeology Crosshair Auto-Tap.png|32x32px]] [[File:Archaeology_Gold_Crosshair_Auto-Tap.png|32x32px]] Crosshair Auto-Taps require [[Archaeology#Ascension|Ascension]] 1 [[Archaeology#tabber-Ascension_1|upgrades]] to be unlocked and can occur in both regular and Gold variants. They show up for around 2 seconds and then disappear, automatically dealing the damage to the block in question in the same way as normal crosshairs would.

===Crosshair Fairy===
[[File:Archaeology_Crosshair_Fairy.png|32x32px]] Crosshair Fairies also require [[Archaeology#Ascension|Ascension]] 1 [[Archaeology#Ascension_1|upgrade]] to be unlocked. After unlocking they can show up randomly, flying around in the Archaeology window. When interacted with they cause Crosshairs to show up on all of the blocks on that stage.

== Idols ==
Idols can be purchased with fragments you acquire and provide buffs to other areas of the game. Idol fragment costs cap out at 999.
Any effects shown between "<code>[ ]</code>" are one time unlocks and not increased when buying more idols of the same type.

Holding the Idol buy button will continuously buy idols, gradually speeding up. Dragging to another buy button will preserve the buying speed increase.

===[[File:Idol Token.png]] Idol Token===
Idol Tokens give you a random Idol, without increasing the cost of Idols. If you don't have any Idols available in a tier, you won't be able to get an Idol from that tier. For example: if all Idols except Divine are maxed, and Divine Idols have been unlocked by ascending, Divine Idols will always roll. You can get Idol Tokens from [[Store#Gifts|gifts]] or a [[Store#Value Packs|Value Pack]].
